verses.1: I love, because the LORD hears my voice, my pleas for mercy.
verses.2: Because he has inclined his ear to me, and in my days I will call.
verses.3: Tangles of death surrounded me, and the straits of Sheol found me. Trouble and sorrow I found.
verses.4: And in the name of the LORD I will call: O LORD, save my life.
verses.5: Gracious and righteous is the LORD, and our God is merciful.
verses.6: The LORD watches over the helpless. I was humbled, and he rescued me.
verses.7: Return, my soul, to your rest, for the LORD has been good to you.
verses.8: For he has delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from stumbling.
verses.9: I will walk before the LORD in the lands of the living.
verses.10: I believed, therefore I spoke. I was greatly comforted.
verses.11: I said in my haste, all people are liars.
verses.12: What shall I return to the LORD for all the goodness he has done to me?
verses.13: I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the LORD.
verses.14: I will fulfill my vows to the LORD, now in the presence of all his people.
verses.15: Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his faithful ones.
verses.16: O LORD, behold, I am your servant. I am your servant, the son of your handmaid. You have loosed my bonds.
verses.17: To you I will offer a thanksgiving sacrifice and call on the name of the LORD.
verses.18: I will fulfill my vows to the LORD, now in the presence of all his people.
verses.19: In the courts of the house of the LORD, in your midst, Jerusalem. Hallelujah.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: The phrase "I believed, therefore I spoke" reflects the Hebrew "הֶאֱמַנְתִּי כִּי אֲדַבֵּר" which is best rendered as a confession of faith leading to speech, not a logical inference.
- v. 19: The Hebrew is ambiguous whether this is the speaker's declaration or an instruction. The translation follows the poetic structure as a declaration.
- v. 16: The phrase "the son of your handmaid" is a poetic way of expressing servitude within a family relationship.
